To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sugar-type surfactants and hybrid liposomes composed with sugar-type surfactant, phospholipid and nonionic surfactant are effective to inhibit the growth of tumor cell lines.

we successfully produced sugar-type surfactants, LacCn, and the three-component hybrid vesicles of LacCn, Tween 20 and DMPC showed remarkable inhibitory effects on the growth of the lung carcinoma cell line.

the sugar surfactant, lactonoalkyamide, was synthesized for the first time, and that three-component hybrid liposome including sugar surfactant exhibited remarkably enhanced inhibitory effects on the growth of cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of sugar-type micellar-type surfactants and the preparation of three-component hybrid lipid vesicles composed of DMPC/Tween 20/LacCn, which exhibit high inhibitory effects on the growth of cancer cells.
the development of sugar-based surfactants, which can form hybrid liposomes and inhibit the growth of tumor (cancer) cells.
the development of novel sugar-type surfactant and the production of three-component hybrid lipid vesicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sugar-type micellar amphiphiles are promising for the development of new drug carriers for the effective delivery of drugs to tumor cells.

sugar surfactant, LacCn, has an important role in the formation of three-component hybrid vesicles with high inhibitory effects on tumor cells, and the inhibitory effects of these vesicles on tumor cells are due to their unique structures.
the three-component hybrid vesicles composed of sugar-type surfactants, Tween 20 and DMPC have a potential for cancer chemotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sugar surfactant, LacCn, is a new type of surfactant that can be used for drug delivery systems.

the three-component hybrid vesicles composed of DMPC and LacCn and Tween 20 were able to inhibit tumor cell growth, and the inhibitory effects of these hybrid vesicles were enhanced remarkably by the addition of Tween 20.

the sugar parts in LacCn play a crucial role to recognize the sugar receptors on the tumor cell membranes and the three-component hybrid vesicles including LacCn can be used as a novel type of drug carrier for cancer therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sugar surfactants are useful for the development of new anticancer agents.
the sugar-type surfactant, LacCn, is a novel component that plays a crucial role in the inhibitory effects of tumor cell growth.
the combination of three components (DMPC, LacCn, Tween 20) in the liposomes plays a key role in the inhibitory effects on the growth of U251 and RERF-LC-AOK cells.
